payload.subject: Mathematics

groupNeeds.need: needs concrete counters and a number line
ready to make up and solve their own problems

changes.before: In pairs, learners add with counters and say the number sentence aloud.
changes.after: Learners add with counters on a number line while the teacher models the first two sums.

changes.before: Observe: can the learner add two small numbers using counters?
changes.after: Observe with a counter set in hand: can the learner add two small numbers?

sections.heading: CAPS reference
sections.text: DEMO s2.1

sections.heading: Learning intention
sections.text: Today we add two small numbers using counters.
sections.sourceRef: typed by the teacher · Learning intention

sections.heading: Success criteria
sections.text:
I can add two small numbers using counters
I can write the answer to an addition

sections.heading: Prior knowledge
sections.text: Learners can count forwards in ones and twos.
sections.sourceRef: typed by the teacher · Prior knowledge

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Show 3 counters and 2 counters. Ask how many there are in all.

sections.heading: Main activity
sections.text: Learners add with counters on a number line while the teacher models the first two sums.

sections.heading: Consolidation
sections.text: Share one number sentence from each pair.

sections.heading: Differentiation
sections.text: Group A uses counters and a number line. Group B adds without counters. Group C writes a story for a sum.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: Observe with a counter set in hand: can the learner add two small numbers?

sections.heading: Resources
sections.text:
Counters, number line.
Low-resource: bottle tops or stones in a tin.
